name: Washington
special_rule: Deaths before 2026-07-01 use a $3,076,000 exclusion and rates up to 35%.

name: Oregon
special_rule: Lowest threshold in the country. Tax is computed on the whole taxable estate once the $1,000,000 threshold is crossed.

name: Illinois
special_rule: Interrelated calculation under the Attorney General's instructions rather than a simple bracket table. Effective marginal rate just above the threshold is roughly 28%.

name: Massachusetts
special_rule: Computed from the former federal state death tax credit table (Table A) less a $99,600 credit, which produces the $2,000,000 effective exemption.

name: Rhode Island
special_rule: Computed from the former federal credit table (Table A) less an $87,940 credit. Exemption is inflation adjusted annually.

name: New York
special_rule: Cliff. The exemption phases out completely once the estate exceeds 105% of the threshold ($7,717,500), and above that point the entire estate is taxed from the first dollar.

name: Connecticut
special_rule: Exemption matches the federal basic exclusion. Flat 12%, with total tax capped at $15,000,000. Connecticut is the only state that also levies its own gift tax.

name: Vermont
special_rule: Flat 16% on the excess over the exemption.

name: District of Columbia
special_rule: Zero bracket amount is inflation adjusted annually.

name: Maryland
special_rule: Only jurisdiction with both taxes. 16% estate tax above $5,000,000 plus a 10% inheritance tax on heirs outside close family. The two are credited against each other.

name: Pennsylvania
special_rule: Taxed from the first dollar with no exemption. Spouses 0%, children and parents 4.5%, siblings 12%, all others 15%.

name: New Jersey
special_rule: Class A (spouse, children, grandchildren, parents) fully exempt. Class C (siblings, children-in-law) 11% to 16% over a $25,000 allowance. Class D (everyone else) 15% to 16% from the first dollar.

name: Kentucky
special_rule: Class A (spouse, children, grandchildren, parents, siblings) fully exempt. Class B (nieces, nephews) 4% to 16% over $1,000. Class C (unrelated) 6% to 16% over $500.

name: Nebraska
special_rule: Levied at county level per beneficiary. Close relatives 1% over $100,000 each, remote relatives 11% over $40,000, all others 15% over $25,000. Heirs under 22 are exempt.
